title: Grammar: Gender: every noun is masculine or feminine
subtitle: Unit 3: Forms and papers

steps.title: Gender: every noun is masculine or feminine
steps.body: All French nouns have a gender, even objects. There is no logic to learn from the meaning, so always learn a noun with its article: not passeport, but le passeport.

steps.title: Articles
rows: the (before a vowel or silent h)

steps.title: Gender: every noun is masculine or feminine
steps.body: Helpful endings (not perfect rules, but they work most of the time):

steps.title: Endings that help
rows: -tion: la signature, la nation, la station
-age: le courrier? no: le message, le passage
most words ending in a consonant: le passeport, le nom

steps.title: Watch out
steps.body: la ville (city) and la maison (house) are feminine; le pays (country) and le nom (name) are masculine. Do not guess from English. When you learn a new noun, say it with its article three times.

steps.title: Tip
steps.body: In a dictionary or list you see n.m. (masculine noun) or n.f. (feminine noun). In this book we write (m.) and (f.) when the article does not show it (l'adresse (f.)).
